policy_title: Increase farming budget and focus on smaller farms
stated: Reform UK will increase the farming budget to £3 billion, focusing on smaller farms, keeping farmland in use, bringing young people into farming, boosting the rural economy and culture, and encouraging innovation and diversification.

source.quote: Increase the Farming Budget to £3 Billion Focus on smaller farms. Keep farmland in use. Bring young people into farming. Boost rural economy and culture. Increase innovation and diversification. Help farmers to farm, not pay them to leave or retire.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly targets rural employment — bringing young people into farming, supporting smaller farms, and boosting the rural economy — directly affecting job creation, income security, and work quality for agricultural workers.
Keeping farmland in use and expanding domestic food production capacity plausibly bears on food costs, an explicit O2 indicator, by affecting domestic supply levels and food security margins.

Commits £3bn in public spending (current UK farming budget ~£2.4bn post-Brexit); a material increase in agricultural expenditure bears on public finances sustainability, especially if funding source is unspecified.
Directly aims to boost the rural economy, encourage innovation and diversification — concrete supply-side and productivity mechanisms that affect aggregate rural living standards and opportunity.

Explicitly prioritises smaller farms over larger agri-businesses, redistributing subsidy incidence within agriculture and addressing regional rural inequality — a clear directional effect on the gap between larger and smaller operators.
Explicitly targets rural culture, community and keeping young people in farming — a direct mechanism for maintaining social cohesion and belonging in rural communities.

membership_note: Policy bears on five fundamentals: it creates direct employment/opportunity effects (O4), a significant public spending commitment (O12), rural economic growth and productivity (O13), redistributive focus on smaller farms narrowing intra-sector and regional inequality (O14), and explicitly targets rural community vitality (O15). No clear non-negligible mechanisms to O1, O2, O3, O5, O6, O7, O8, O9, O10 or O11 — food price effects (O2) are too diffuse given global commodity dominance; environmental conditions (O6) are not specified in the stated policy.
